Fig.2Dcompares several measures across the experiments. It shows that generative agents with information about prevalence are able to bring down the number of cumulative cases and the maximum number of cases by lowering their own mobility, while their reactions double the epidemic duration.

Fig. 2. Comparison of simulation results from three experimental conditions with a 100-agent population. Panels (A-C): average daily cases and mobility (and their 80% confidence interval with dashed line) as well as four samples of simulation (darker lines are 3-day moving average) for (A) the first condition with no health information to agents, (B) when own-health information is provided, and (C) when own health and societal health information is provided. Panel (D) compares cumulative cases, average mobility, largest peak in cases, and epidemic duration across the three experimental conditions.
